## Process lifecycle

- Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
- Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
- After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.

## Linux browser and WebGPU capture

- Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
- Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
- Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
- Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
- Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
- Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
- Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
- Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
- Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.

## Mobile browser games

- Support Android and iOS phones and tablets with responsive layouts and usable touch controls.
- Keep gameplay and controls visible within safe areas and avoid browser gesture conflicts.
- Add tilt controls only when appropriate; offer touch alternatives and request iOS motion permission from a user gesture when needed.
- Follow explicit device and control requirements in the user request.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Start the saved project and publish readiness only after both HTTP checks pass.
set -euo pipefail
cd "${PROJECT_DIR:?}"
: "${OPENCODE_WEB_DIR:?}" "${APP_URL:?}"
PORT="${APP_PORT:-3000}"
export PORT
startup_timeout="${STARTUP_TIMEOUT_SECONDS:-600}"
[[ "$startup_timeout" =~ ^[1-9][0-9]*$ ]] || { echo 'STARTUP_TIMEOUT_SECONDS must be a positive integer.' >&2; exit 1; }
/usr/bin/time -p test -f start.sh
/usr/bin/time -p bash -n start.sh
current_commit="${CHECKPOINT_COMMIT:-}"
previous_commit=""
[[ ! -f "$OPENCODE_WEB_DIR/served-commit" ]] || previous_commit="$(/usr/bin/time -p cat "$OPENCODE_WEB_DIR/served-commit")"
# Reuse an in-flight build for this checkpoint when a readiness retry returns.
starting=false
if [[ -f "$OPENCODE_WEB_DIR/starting-commit" ]] && [[ "$(/usr/bin/time -p cat "$OPENCODE_WEB_DIR/starting-commit")" == "$current_commit" ]] && /usr/bin/time -p tmux has-session -t app-server 2>/dev/null; then
  starting=true
fi
if [[ "${RESTART_APP:-false}" == true ]] || { [[ "$starting" == false ]] && { [[ -n "$current_commit" && "$previous_commit" != "$current_commit" ]] || ! /usr/bin/time -p curl --fail --silent --max-time 3 "http://127.0.0.1:$PORT/" >/dev/null; }; }; then
  /usr/bin/time -p rm -f "$OPENCODE_WEB_DIR/ready-preview-url"
  /usr/bin/time -p tmux kill-session -t app-server 2>/dev/null || true
  /usr/bin/time -p node "${RUNTIME_DIR:?}/scripts/reclaim-preview-port.mjs"
  /usr/bin/time -p /usr/bin/printf '%s' "$current_commit" > "$OPENCODE_WEB_DIR/starting-commit"
  # Pass paths through tmux's environment; keep the script in the foreground.
  /usr/bin/time -p tmux new-session -d -s app-server -c "$PROJECT_DIR" \
    -e "RUNTIME_DIR=${RUNTIME_DIR:?}" -e "OPENCODE_WEB_DIR=$OPENCODE_WEB_DIR" -e "PORT=$PORT" -e "STARTUP_LOG=$OPENCODE_WEB_DIR/app.log" \
    'bash start.sh > "$STARTUP_LOG" 2>&1'
fi
ready=false
for ((attempt=0; attempt<(startup_timeout + 1) / 2; attempt++)); do
  /usr/bin/time -p tmux has-session -t app-server 2>/dev/null || { echo 'Startup process exited. Inspect app.log.' >&2; exit 1; }
  if /usr/bin/time -p curl --fail --silent --max-time 3 "http://127.0.0.1:$PORT/" >/dev/null; then
    ready=true
    break
  fi
  /usr/bin/time -p tmux has-session -t app-server 2>/dev/null || { echo 'Startup process exited. Inspect app.log.' >&2; exit 1; }
  /usr/bin/time -p sleep 2
done
[[ "$ready" == true ]] || { echo "Local startup failed after ${startup_timeout}s. Inspect app.log." >&2; exit 75; }
/usr/bin/time -p rm -f "$OPENCODE_WEB_DIR/starting-commit"
# Local readiness is independent of a temporary public tunnel failure.
/usr/bin/time -p /usr/bin/printf '%s' "$current_commit" > "$OPENCODE_WEB_DIR/served-commit"
for ((attempt=0; attempt<12; attempt++)); do
  status="$(/usr/bin/time -p curl --silent --show-error --location --max-time 10 --output "$OPENCODE_WEB_DIR/public-readiness.log" --write-out '%{http_code}' "$APP_URL")" || status=000
  if [[ "$status" == 2* ]]; then
    /usr/bin/time -p /usr/bin/printf '%s' "$APP_URL" > "$OPENCODE_WEB_DIR/ready-preview-url"
    if [[ -n "${OPENCODE_CONTROL_PORT:-}" ]]; then
      /usr/bin/time -p curl --fail --silent --max-time 5 "http://127.0.0.1:$OPENCODE_CONTROL_PORT/omgithub/heartbeat" >/dev/null || true
    fi
    echo 'Local and public preview are ready.'
    exit 0
  fi
  if [[ "$status" == 4* && "$status" != 408 && "$status" != 429 ]]; then
    echo "Public preview rejected the request (HTTP $status). Inspect public-readiness.log." >&2
    exit 1
  fi
  /usr/bin/time -p sleep 2
done
echo 'Public preview did not become ready.' >&2
exit 75

export function landscapeHeight(x,z){
  const az=Math.abs(z);

  const side = z<0 ? 1 : 0.42;

## Objective
- Build a 3D low-poly mobile-friendly browser game inspired by Hill Climb Racing, with driving over procedural hills, coins, fuel, flips, garage, and polished HUD/menu.

## Requirements
- User request, verbatim: `"3д низкополигональная игра в духе hill climv racing"`
- Support Android/iOS phones and tablets with responsive layouts and usable touch controls; keep controls within safe areas; offer touch alternatives to tilt (no tilt needed).
- Must be visually verified in a real browser; reject blank/loading screens; report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering, not GPU acceleration.
- Original branding/assets; no copyrighted Hill Climb Racing assets or names.

## Decisions
- Built as static HTML/CSS/ES modules served from repo root; no `package.json` (runtime serves `index.html` directly).
- Vendored Three.js r180 (`vendor/three.module.js` + `vendor/three.module.min.core` dependency) and local Bungee/Outfit fonts for offline reliability.
- Game name: **Ridge Rush 3D**.
- Custom 2D side-view arcade vehicle physics (spring suspension, terrain chassis collision, air rotation via gas/brake) rendered in 3D with dynamic chase camera.
- Procedural endless terrain, trees/rocks/flowers via instancing, coin arcs, fuel cans every ~240m, distance signs every 100m, starting gate at x=16.
- Three unlockable vehicles: Trail Jeep (free), Dune Buggy (220 coins), Mud Titan (520 coins); localStorage save key `ridgeRush3d.save.v1`.
- Procedural WebAudio engine/SFX; mute persistence.
- Desktop controls: arrows/WASD, `R` restart, `M` mute; mobile: two large on-screen pedals.

## Work State
### Completed
- Full game implementation across `index.html`, `styles.css`, `js/main.js`, `js/world.js`, `js/vehicle.js`, `js/audio.js`.
- Procedural world, sky, mountains, clouds, terrain chunks, props, coins, fuel, signs, gate.
- Vehicle physics/model for 3 vehicles; collisions, flips, fuel, coin pickup, crashes, results, garage, save/load, audio, particles.
- Fixed initial black-screen bug caused by `car.z` undefined → NaN camera position; added `this.z = 0` in `Vehicle.reset`.
- Fixed missing Three.js dependency `vendor/three.core.min.js` (404).
- Fixed coin spawning to include the start chunk; coin pickup now verified (`coins: 3` at x=14).
- Improved visuals: pastel cloud clusters, unfogged blue mountain ridges, softer/smoother terrain colors with wheel ruts, denser forest.
- Adjusted portrait chase camera and mobile hint; mobile car is now fully visible.
- Menu camera repositioned: desktop car sits right-of-center; mobile car small in upper area.
- Desktop and mobile renders confirmed working under Playwright/SwiftShader; screenshots generated.

### Active
- Final visual polish and verification: inspect latest menu/gameplay screenshots, tune remaining composition/readability issues.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Review latest screenshots (`screenshots/menu-desktop.png`, `play-desktop.png`, `menu-mobile.png`, `play-mobile.png`, `run-*.png`) for composition and any remaining visual defects.
2. Verify mobile touch pedals actually drive the car and multi-touch does not stick; test at 390×844 and maybe landscape.
3. Test gameplay across hills for crashes/flips/fuel/results/garage flows; ensure no console errors.
4. Possibly reduce giant pale far-mountain/cloud shapes and further soften terrain banding if still noticeable.
5. Run the official capture flow (`capture.sh` / `default-capture.mjs`) and confirm desktop/mobile final screenshots are non-blank, no page errors, and HUD visible.
6. Commit changes when satisfied.

## Relevant Files
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/index.html`: DOM, overlays, HUD, garage, results markup.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/styles.css`: full responsive UI, menu, garage, HUD, touch controls, animations.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/js/main.js`: scene/renderer setup, state machine, input, camera, particles, garage, save, UI wiring, debug `window.__ridgeRush`.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/js/world.js`: terrain functions, chunks, sky/lights/mountains/clouds, props, pickups, gate.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/js/vehicle.js`: vehicle configs, procedural models, suspension/physics, crash/flip events.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/js/audio.js`: procedural WebAudio engine and SFX.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/vendor/three.module.js`: vendored Three.js r180.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/vendor/three.core.min.js`: required Three.js core dependency.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/assets/fonts/bungee-latin.woff2`: title font.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/assets/fonts/outfit-latin.woff2`: UI font.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/screenshots/`: current Playwright verification images.
- `/tmp/opencode/test2.js`: desktop/mobile screenshot + run-state test.
- `/tmp/opencode/test-game.js`: longer drive test.
- `/tmp/opencode/debug3.js`: renderer/camera diagnostic.
- `/tmp/opencode/app.log`: local server log.

## Important Context
- Local server running in tmux session `app-server` on `http://127.0.0.1:3002/` via `node "$RUNTIME_DIR/scripts/default-start.mjs"`.
- Playwright launch config: `/home/runner/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json`; use `chromium.launch({ ...config.browser.launchOptions })` with `DISPLAY` from `~/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/display`.
- Capture harness auto-clicks only a visible button whose text exactly matches `PLAY`; only one such button exists.
- `page.goto(..., { waitUntil: 'load' })` waits for module top-level `await document.fonts.ready`, so button listeners are bound before capture clicks.
- Debug API: `window.__ridgeRush` exposes `state`, `car`, `run`, `save`, `world`, `renderer`, `scene`, `camera`, `startRun`, `finishRun`, `goMenu`.
- Physics uses fixed substeps; `car.z` must remain 0; camera must never receive undefined coordinates.
- Current last test results: desktop menu camera `[6.5, 6.16, 18.02]`; desktop play cam `[-6.66, 5.6, 15.92]`; mobile menu cam `[8.77, 7.58, 23.79]`; mobile play cam `[-6.37, 5.72, 16.81]`.
- Latest run state: desktop x=14, coins=3, fuel=97.7, speed=12.7, no crash; mobile x=45.7, coins=4, fuel=94.5, speed=14.5, no crash.
- All changes are uncommitted in the working tree; initial repo commit is `9d596e5`.
- Existing visual concerns from latest screenshots: menu desktop looks good; play desktop has a large pale/glacier-like far mountain mass at top-left, but overall scene is readable; mobile menu composition now acceptable.
- The runtime uses SwiftShader CPU software rendering; do not claim hardware GPU acceleration.

## Process lifecycle

- Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
- Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
- After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.

## Linux browser and WebGPU capture

- Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
- Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
- Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
- Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
- Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
- Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
- Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
- Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
- Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.

## Mobile browser games

- Support Android and iOS phones and tablets with responsive layouts and usable touch controls.
- Keep gameplay and controls visible within safe areas and avoid browser gesture conflicts.
- Add tilt controls only when appropriate; offer touch alternatives and request iOS motion permission from a user gesture when needed.
- Follow explicit device and control requirements in the user request.

## Что реализовано
- 3D low-poly гонка по бесконечным процедурным холмам в духе hill climb racing.
- Физика с подвеской, прыжками, сальто, опрокидыванием и валунами.
- Монеты, канистры с топливом, указатели дистанции, стартовые ворота.
- Три машины: Trail Jeep, Dune Buggy, Mud Titan — покупка/выбор в гараже.
- HUD: дистанция, рекорд, монеты, топливо, спидометр.
- Процедурный звук двигателя и SFX, сохранение прогресса и mute в `localStorage`.
- Адаптивный интерфейс для телефонов и планшетов, крупные педали GAS/BRAKE, поддержка мультитача.
- Оригинальный брендинг и ассеты, без материалов Hill Climb Racing.

## Проверено в браузере
- Меню, заезд, авария, экран результатов, гонка «до топлива», гараж и покупка машины.
- Мобильное управление реальными touch-событиями: газ, тормоз, одновременное нажатие и независимое отпускание.
- Разрешения: 320×568, 375×667, 390×844, 768×1024, 1024×768, 1440×900 — без переполнений и обрезанных кнопок.
- Сохранение прогресса после перезагрузки.
- Ошибок в консоли нет; официальный capture-flow прошёл.

Рендер проверялся в Chromium на **SwiftShader — это программный CPU-рендеринг, не аппаратное GPU-ускорение**. На реальных телефонах сцена лёгкая: ~59 draw calls и ~15k треугольников.
